What is the difference between range() in Python 2 and Python 3?

Supplied answer
In Python 2 range() built a full list in memory and xrange() returned a lazy iterator. In Python 3, xrange()
is gone and range() itself is lazy - it produces values on demand, so range(10**8) uses almost no
memory. Wrap it in list() if you actually need a list.
